before: In suggesting mode, inserting or deleting a table column, and deleting a selection that covered a whole table, wrote untracked edits. Rejecting a proposed table that its author had typed into was refused.
after: They write Word tracked markup: w:cellIns or w:cellDel on each cell of the column, and w:del and w:cellDel on every row of a covered table. Rejecting a proposed row, cell, or table, or accepting a proposed deletion of one, also resolves the same author's pending changes inside it.
reason: Only the markup a local edit writes, and which sites one review decision selects, change. Released replicas already preserve, replay, and resolve these cell and row revision forms when they come from a file, and a decision still travels as the ordinary resolution of the sites it names. Shared nodes, identities, offsets, and synchronization stay unchanged.
